articles.title: Saved for Sunday: How Sarah J Maas became romantasy’s Taylor Swift
articles.summary: I didn’t leave the house at all last weekend. Instead, I spent Saturday smashing A Court of Splintered Harmony and Sunday watching BookToks about it. In this week’s newsletter, senior podcast producer Taylah Strano quizzes me about the Maasverse and the rise of romantasy.
body: Leading questions: My upbringing was not full of leisure activities. How can I model a joyful life for my kids?

Taylah: Who is Sarah J Maas? Alyx: Sarah J Maas is basically the Taylor Swift of romantasy. A Court of Splintered Harmony, the sixth book in her biggest series, A Court of Thorns and Roses, sold 1.7m copies worldwide on pre-order and on the first day of sale. There were midnight parties all over the world for the release. So her sexy fairy novels – and when I say sexy I mean there are sex scenes that last for 10 pages or longer – are keeping publishing afloat right now. Unfortunately, from my perspective and many of her other fans’, if she is Taylor Swift, this is her The Life of a Showgirl (it’s not very good).

Instead, I spent Saturday smashing A Court of Splintered Harmony and Sunday watching BookToks about it.

articles.title: ‘I’m walking up hills!’ Maggie Beer on recovery, young fans and 20 years since the Cook and the Chef
articles.summary: Ahead of her talk at the Powerhouse Parramatta Opening festival, the 81-year-old cookbook author and presenter says she still has a lot on her plate. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email.
body: I t has been 20 years since the first episode of the Cook and the Chef aired in 2006, introducing Australian viewers to culinary odd couple Maggie Beer and Simon Bryant. Each episode the pair gently ribbed each other in Beer’s cottagecore kitchen in the Barossa Valley, then turned out dishes such as bruschetta, grilled kingfish and olive tapenade.
The show served up 154 episodes over four seasons – and who knows how many litres of verjuice. But there was a moment, in pre-production, when it seemed like the series wouldn’t get off the ground.

As Beer remembers it, their first trial in front of the camera was “hopeless”; they were riddled with nerves. But once the cameras were turned off, she and Bryant “sat on the steps afterwards and just talked and talked, and laughed and laughed, about how hopeless it had been”, and their executive producer could see their real-life chemistry. In the next few sessions on-set, their combined charisma and mutual love for cooking meant “we forgot the camera was there”, Beer says.
points: Ahead of her talk at the Powerhouse Parramatta Opening festival, the 81-year-old cookbook author and presenter says she still has a lot on her plate.

articles.title: The moment I knew: He said he was having a midlife crisis – I saw a man willing to face his fears
articles.summary: Performer Jeremy Lloyd had a rule: no dating within the theatre and dance industry. He broke that rule with David. Find more stories from the moment I knew series. When David and I met, we’d both recently come out of long-term relationships and had our lives reorganised by the reality of mortality.
body: In early 2018 I was in my mid-20s, living in Sydney, and had just returned to dancing and performing after a three-year hiatus.
I joined the dating apps seeking affirmation that I could be desired again, and explicitly stated my HIV status on my profile.

Because my previous partners had been dance or theatre people, I had made a soft rule to not date within the industry. I broke that rule with David, although I didn’t realise it at the start of our first date.

That night, we drank two bottles of wine in his apartment and talked for hours. We covered everything from Netflix shows to movies we’d seen – intentionally avoiding talking about work. It wasn’t until I got up to go to the bathroom that I noticed the posters lining the wall. Productions he had worked on as a stage manager: Priscilla, Strictly Ballroom, West Side Story.
points: Performer Jeremy Lloyd had a rule: no dating within the theatre and dance industry.

articles.title: In defense of feral children
articles.summary: Adults complain and say kids should occupy more space in the world. Then when they do, the world tells them to quiet down. On the Maine island where I live, childhood ends when you’re old enough to catch the 7.15am ferry to school.
body: We live year-round on Peaks Island, a small island accessible only by boat about 3 miles off the coast of Portland. There is an elementary school here, but no middle or high school. So, once island children reach sixth grade, they begin commuting to the mainland by ferry. In many ways, it is a rite of passage.

When my son Theo started middle school, I was thrilled for him – and a little heartbroken. Suddenly, he was across the bay all day, reachable only by boat or cellphone (which he didn’t have). Theo has always belonged to our island as much as he has belonged to me. After years of rinsing sand from his socks and pulling twigs from his hair, sending him away each morning felt a little like prying him loose from his natural habitat.
Fortunately, my son’s daily commute across Casco Bay suggests he has not yet been entirely domesticated.
points: Adults complain and say kids should occupy more space in the world.
Then when they do, the world tells them to quiet down.

articles.title: Beauty Marks: The Best Beauty Looks of the Week
articles.summary: From Sienna Miller’s romantic blurred lip to Kate Young’s diamond-studded chignon, this week’s best beauty looks were all in the details.
body: Welcome back to Beauty Marks: Vogue ’s weekly edition of the best moments in celebrity beauty, from Vogue editors’ IG feeds, and all the glam of the fashion and pop culture landscapes. Each week, we curate the nail art to pin for your next nail appointment, new recruits to ‘Team Bob’, and major red carpet moments from the week’s most glamorous affairs. As always, it’s as much about celebrity beauty as it is about the makeup artists, hairstylists, and nail artists, as well as the creators crafting the trends you’re about to see everywhere.

This week in beauty was a study in contrasts: sculptural hair met soft-focus makeup, while barely-there lips shared the spotlight with high-impact eyes. Sienna Miller made a romantic case for the blurred lip, Emily Blunt embraced a wintry shade of blonde, and Kim Petras dialed up the drama with graphic liner and ice-blonde bangs. Elsewhere, Kate Young turned a diamond into the ultimate hair accessory, Kris Jenner revisited the razor-sharp bob, and Lily Allen served up a masterclass in hair transformations. From elaborate nail art to gravity-defying chignons, there was plenty to look twice at.
points: From Sienna Miller’s romantic blurred lip to Kate Young’s diamond-studded chignon, this week’s best beauty looks were all in the details.

articles.title: A Costa Rican Beach Resort with a World-Class Coffee Program
articles.summary: The roastery at Nekajui on the Papagayo Peninsula shows off the country’s rich coffee culture.
body: In Hotels With Great Taste, we’re pulling back the curtain for a peek at the “special sauce” that hotels use to create memorable, meaningful culinary experiences for their guests.

Check-in at Nekajui on Costa Rica’s verdant Papagayo Peninsula happens inside a sparsely furnished bungalow the staff call La Casita. But walk across the drive, past a massive ceiba tree hung heavy with lanterns, and all humility vanishes. The whole property sweeps out before you: an endless green lawn, pools cascading down two levels, and, finally, the serenely sparkling bay beyond.

Nekajui is Ritz Carlton’s first Reserve resort in Central or South America. The Reserve’s are Ritz Carlton’s nod to the idea of complete escape, often in the far flung retreats—the Chinese Himalayas, or the Saudi Arabian desert.

Now, the recently opened Nekajui allows you to unwind on the lush Costa Rican coast teeming with wildlife like capuchins, coatis, and iguanas. Hidden away at the remote property, you’ll also find a local coffee program that’s on par with the best big city cafes in the world.
points: The roastery at Nekajui on the Papagayo Peninsula shows off the country’s rich coffee culture.

articles.title: 20 Food Advent Calendars to Buy Before They Sell Out (2026)
articles.summary: From cookies and chocolates to wine and cheese, these are the best food advent calendars to buy in 2026.
body: Nothing sparks joy and jumpstarts the Christmas season like a food advent calendar. You get 25 tiny compartments, each housing a festive treat hidden behind a perforated door. They’re not just chocolate anymore. These days, they’re filled with everything from gummies and chili crisp to whiskey and coffee. And if you’re thinking of ordering one to enjoy this year, the time is now. December 1st is only seven weeks away, and after reporting on these things for the past five years, we’ve seen these calendars sell out months in advance or get backordered every year.

The best advent calendars contain high-quality sweets, booze, condiments, snacks, teas, or coffees you’ll be genuinely excited to open every day. And who knows, they might even introduce you to a product you’ll want to buy on repeat once the holiday season has come and gone.

articles.title: Dry Brushing: Why I Do It Every Day And All The Benefits
articles.summary: Dry body brushing has long been touted by celebrities as a wellness ritual to try for enhanced lymphatic drainage and more even skin tone. But does it work? We tested to see.
body: It seems like every time I watch a get-ready-with-me video, the first step of the routine is dry brushing. And while I’ve tried it here and there, I never found myself committing to the act. But this skin-care practice is beloved by not only the likes of Gwyneth Paltrow and Tracee Ellis Ross, but also by functional health doctors and medical professionals as well.

So what is dry brushing? It’s the act of running a bristled brush across your skin while working against gravity (so working toward your torso on limbs) to help with moving the body’s lymphatic system.

Everybody raves about the myriad of health benefits that comes along with dry brushing—from physically exfoliating your skin and eliminating strawberry skin to increasing blood flow and potentially diminishing the appearance of circulation.
